definitions.explanation: a scholar who studies and practices Confucian philosophy, especially in the context of pre-modern East Asian intellectual history

examples.japanese: ⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{儒者|じゅしゃ}がいた。
examples.english: There were many Confucian scholars during the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {儒者|じゅしゃ}たち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{藩|はん}→藩：14124_han⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{政治|せいじ}→政治：01629_seiji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{影響|えいきょう}→影響：01877_eikyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}えた→与える：01821_ataeru⟧。
examples.english: Confucian scholars also had a great influence on domain politics.

examples.japanese: ⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{儒者|じゅしゃ}⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧{荻生徂徠|おぎゅうそらい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{独自|どくじ}→独自：05614_dokuji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{学問|がくもん}→学問：02604_gakumon⟧⟦{体系|たいけい}→体系：04487_taikei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{築|きず}いた→築く：02046_kizuku⟧。
examples.english: The famous Confucian scholar Ogyu Sorai established his own system of learning.

notes:
Refers specifically to scholars of Confucianism ({儒学|じゅがく}), a philosophical tradition originating in China that emphasizes ethics, social harmony, and proper governance. In Japan, Confucian scholars were particularly influential during the Edo period (1603-1868), when the Tokugawa shogunate adopted Neo-Confucianism as its official ideology.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {儒者|じゅしゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{教|おし}え→教え：01909_oshie⟧: teachings of Confucian scholars
- {儒者|じゅしゃ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{仕|つか}える→仕える：11547_tsukaeru⟧: to serve as a Confucian scholar/advisor
- ⟦{御用|ごよう}→御用：12848_goyou⟧{儒者|じゅしゃ}: a Confucian scholar in official government service

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {儒学者|じゅがくしゃ}: Confucian scholar — a synonymous but slightly more formal compound
- ⟦{学者|がくしゃ}→学者：02544_gakusha⟧: scholar — a general term for any academic or learned person
- {朱子学者|しゅしがくしゃ}: Neo-Confucian scholar — specifically a follower of Zhu Xi's school of thought
- {国学者|こくがくしゃ}: scholar of National Learning — scholars who studied Japan's native traditions as a counterpoint to Chinese Confucianism
